title: Coverage of a mixed recipient bed

cues.phrase: currently exposed central tendon
cues.why: The task selects the decisive exhibit row for the learner. The peripheral granulation and prior template can be deleted without changing this direct bare-tendon coverage question.

cues.phrase: Flap coverage of the central defect
cues.why: The key is the only flap against two graft-thickness variants. This category outlier offers a test-taking hint, although knowing why the grafts fail still requires medical knowledge.

fairness: Flap coverage is the defensible best of these three direct-coverage choices for tendon explicitly lacking paratenon and a granulation covering. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
This is a standalone node. The problem is difficulty, not absence of a necessary negative; retain the actual central-bed observations.

Review scope for this report: all 29 candidate nodes, comprising six rewritten versions and 23 new versions. Nine Keep and 32 Retire-and-replace inventory records, historical holds, and the unkeyed clean/completed-series hold were noted but not reviewed as executable candidates. Seven Rewrite inventory records consolidate to six versions. Judgments use candidate visible fields and prior candidate explanations, not author self-checks. Review was offline; source currency, runtime rendering/waits and clinical approval are not certified. Difficulty and high-yield labels are qualitative judgments, not measured performance or verified exam frequencies.
suggestions: Ask for a plan for the whole defect without identifying the decisive central structure in the task, and compare credible plans whose suitability changes with the distribution of the observed surfaces.
Replace one graft-thickness foil with a clinician-supported competing staged strategy only if visible findings can establish one best next step; do not invent criteria to exclude it.

title: Coverage after recipient-bed preparation
fairness: The current continuous adherent bleeding layer supports grafting despite the historical denuded cortex; marked approximation tension separately defeats direct closure. Repeating the template is less appropriate given the current surface. One defensible best answer is supplied.
The bed and edge observations are decision-critical findings, not gratuitous exclusions. The learner must update the historical assessment and select coverage using current geometry.

Standalone chronology is coherent. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. PASS is editorial and does not establish that any particular prepared bed is clinically ready or confer clinician approval.

title: Fluid beneath a skin graft
clarityIssues: The task is intelligible, but 'early postoperative' does not establish the interval of separation or the lifted segment's viability; an intact epithelial surface alone is not a complete viability assessment.

cues.phrase: new collection beneath
cues.why: The task names the actionable problem and directly matches 'Evacuate the collection'.

cues.phrase: Excise the sheet
cues.why: Both distractors begin with the same destructive action despite an explicitly adherent remainder. The key is the sole preservation option.

fairness: Prompt evacuation and restored contact are reasonable for a newly recognized localized collection; the offered whole-sheet replacements are poor competitors.

Do not teach that an intact epithelial surface guarantees a salvageable graft. The clinical ranking is plausible, but the extent of viability should be clearer if salvage versus replacement is the actual objective.
Standalone retrospective review is coherent; no prior answer contributes difficulty.
suggestions: Use a neutral next-intervention task and retain only observations needed to assess the interface and tissue viability.
Compare plausible local salvage or failure-management plans at the same scope, with a supported observation distinguishing them; avoid two whole-sheet excision foils.

title: Movement-associated graft separation

cues.phrase: The graft lies flat when the wrist is supported.
cues.why: The update practically demonstrates the keyed treatment before the choice.

cues.phrase: recurrent movement-related graft separation
cues.why: The task supplies the causal interpretation that should be inferred from the dynamic observations.

cues.phrase: no recurrent fluid pocket
cues.why: This explicitly deletes the fluid-exploration competitor, leaving a movement/support match against an unmotivated thicker graft.

fairness: Fixation and immobilization fit the described shear; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The exclusion of a recurrent collection is useful clinically, but this option set turns it into direct elimination.
The standalone presentation supplies the prior evacuation, so it does not require completion of the separate fluid node.
suggestions: Remove the causal label from the task and consolidate the duplicated update/exhibit observations.
Build a real distinction between fixation failure, a new interface problem and recipient-bed failure using supported findings and credible competing interventions.

title: Graft selection after finger contracture release
fairness: The learner must integrate the vascular recipient bed and restored extension with the consequences of secondary contraction across a flexion crease. A full-thickness graft is the defensible best offered graft; the donor geometry addresses its practical limitation.
The two thin split-thickness alternatives are weaker but represent plausible thickness/meshing errors. The unmeshed component is shared with one distractor; it does not uniquely reveal the key.

The task appropriately asks which graft, not which reconstruction of every possible kind. The standalone case is coherent. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; exact operative suitability still requires clinician review.

title: Closure of a full-thickness graft donor site

cues.phrase: The viable wound edges approximate without blanching or excessive tension.
cues.why: This provides a near-complete direct-closure eligibility statement; the prior thigh history is unnecessary to select closure of the current wound.

fairness: Direct closure is best among the offered options for this mobile, viable donor wound. The explanation correctly distinguishes retained dermal appendages at the earlier partial-thickness donor site.

The observation is clinically necessary if comparing closure with grafting, so removing it without replacing the decision structure would create ambiguity. It currently supports a foundational rule rather than two consequential steps.
Standalone framing is coherent and avoids needing the separate graft-selection node.
suggestions: Either seek explicit acceptance as a basic donor-site teaching item or redesign around a genuine donor-site planning constraint with credible alternatives.
Retain enough edge/defect information for fairness; do not create difficulty simply by withholding whether closure is feasible.

title: Functional examination after a palmar finger cut
clarityIssues: 'Isolated resisted tendon examination' is less concrete than naming the relevant isolated flexor functions; 'composite grip excursion examination' is awkward terminology.

cues.phrase: could form a loose composite fist
cues.why: This already supplies the composite-movement finding that one distractor proposes to obtain.

cues.phrase: passive motion was full
cues.why: This already supplies the other distractor's result. The key is uniquely the examination not yet documented.

cues.phrase: hurt when pulling firmly
cues.why: Combined with the two completed tests, this directly points to the only resisted test.

fairness: Focused tendon assessment is appropriate despite preserved composite movement. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The first node stands alone, but the choice set makes its inference largely a completed-versus-uncompleted checklist.
suggestions: Compare concrete, equally uncompleted examination maneuvers and use anatomy and functional findings to make one informative.
Have a clinician verify the exact maneuver wording and its role alongside the required neurovascular and wound examination.

title: Disposition with possible occult flexor injury
clarityIssues: The update calls the wound exploration 'completed', while the exhibit says the deep flexor surface could not be fully visualized. Distinguish a completed limited attempt from adequate exploration.

cues.phrase: Protective splint with prompt hand-surgery assessment
cues.why: This is the sole protective, prompt specialist plan against two routine follow-up plans after unresolved painful weakness.

cues.phrase: Small skin wounds and a loose fist do not establish that a tendon is intact.
cues.why: The preceding node's explanation rehearses the central inference this follow-up claims to test.

fairness: Protection and prompt specialist assessment are appropriate for the unresolved injury; a normal radiograph does not establish tendon integrity.

The current findings make the task understandable using the shared case presentation, and the sequence is clinically coherent. Its prior teaching and routine-delay foils substantially lower independent difficulty.
suggestions: Compare real remaining diagnostic/disposition choices at the same urgency rather than prompt referral versus routine delay.
Clarify the limited exploration and test a new consequential distinction not already supplied by the first explanation; preserve any safety-recognition role explicitly if accepted.

title: Tetanus prophylaxis after a dirty wound with completed series
fairness: Soil exposure, the completed primary series, the six-year interval and the immune history support vaccine without TIG. The four balanced combinations require separate active- and passive-prophylaxis decisions without component-convergence cueing.

The vaccine record resolves a different decision from the preceding hand examination and disposition nodes. This update supplies all prophylaxis-critical information, so it stands alone within the shared presentation.
No confident clinical inaccuracy identified from offline knowledge; this is not a fresh verification of guidance.

title: Tetanus prophylaxis with an undocumented primary series
fairness: A recalled injection several years earlier does not establish a completed series. Combined with the soil-contaminated puncture, vaccine plus TIG is the defensible best of the four balanced combinations.
The learner must interpret the sufficiency of the immunization history and then choose active and passive prophylaxis for the wound category. Cleansing does not erase the original exposure.
The retrospective task clearly targets the documented encounter rather than an unspecified decision today. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.

title: Tetanus prophylaxis for a clean wound during a primary series
clarityIssues: 'Had started but had not completed' gives neither dose timing nor whether the next valid primary-series dose is due at the encounter.
The explanation's 'disputed completed-series clean-wound booster interval' refers to an editorial/source dispute absent from the learner's question.

cues.phrase: superficial clean-wound encounter
cues.why: The task repeats the wound classification after the exhibit already names it and lists the exclusions. This is a direct pathway lookup, not an independent wound-classification inference.

fairness: No TIG for the described clean minor wound is defensible. Whether to administer another active dose now cannot be fully resolved from an incomplete-series label alone if a dose was very recent. This is missing scheduling information, not a claim that the intended vaccine recommendation is inherently wrong.
The balanced options avoid convergence; the standalone narrative is otherwise coherent. Do not create an invented interval to repair the missing information.
suggestions: Supply a verified dose history sufficient to establish that the next dose is due, or explicitly ask about completion of active immunization rather than immediate administration.
Remove internal source-dispute commentary from feedback and teach only the clean-wound/TIG distinction and the indicated vaccine-series action.
After the fairness repair, seek basic-purpose acceptance or introduce a real competing prophylaxis error without adding unnecessary narrative.

title: Tetanus immune-globulin exception in HIV

cues.phrase: despite the recent vaccine record
cues.why: The task announces that the recent vaccination does not settle prophylaxis and primes the immune exception. This is an avoidable answer-directed qualifier.

fairness: The intended TIG-without-vaccine answer is consistent with the HIV dirty-wound exception and the recent completed vaccine series. Antiretroviral treatment does not itself remove that exception. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.
The four balanced combinations preserve two independent decisions; the vignette is self-contained. The needed repair is narrow and does not require removing the HIV history.
suggestions: Use a neutral task asking which tetanus prophylaxis was indicated at the wound encounter, deleting 'despite the recent vaccine record'. Preserve the actual wound, vaccination and HIV findings.

title: Nutrient assessment in poor healing and bleeding
clarityIssues: Presentation and current update repeat the slow wound/food-diary encounter almost verbatim.

cues.phrase: routine coagulation studies are within their laboratory reference ranges
cues.why: This directly weakens 'Repeat prothrombin time and INR' without a change or inadequacy that would motivate repeating it.

cues.phrase: almost no fruit or vegetables
cues.why: Alongside gingival bleeding and petechiae, this supplies the classic deficiency association. The shortcut partly requires medical knowledge, but the option set does not make the inference consequential beyond naming its assay.

fairness: Targeted vitamin C assessment is reasonable for the stated constellation; zinc deficiency is a weaker explanation of the bleeding pattern. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
Recognition of scurvy followed by selection of its concentration test is one recall chain under the owner standard. The standalone node does not establish two consequential steps.
suggestions: Remove the duplicate clinic sentence and replace the repeat-normal-test foil with a credible competing assessment.
Test a supported interpretive or management consequence of the findings, or request acceptance as foundational deficiency recognition; do not fabricate laboratory limitations or treatment rules.

title: Investigation of a dressing-associated eruption
clarityIssues: 'Appeared after the procedure' does not specify onset sufficiently to support the explanation's delayed classification. Eczematous morphology supports the intended direction, but actual chronology should be stated.

cues.phrase: rectangular outline of the adhesive dressing
cues.why: Only one option tests 'dressing and adhesive allergens'; neither distractor addresses the visibly implicated materials in the same way.

cues.phrase: Paired serum tryptase testing around the next procedure
cues.why: This proposes testing around a future uneventful procedure instead of investigating the prior eruption, making it a conspicuously weak and differently timed alternative.

fairness: Relevant patch testing is defensible for this eczematous exposure pattern. The footprint does not by itself distinguish every allergic from irritant mechanism, and the explanation appropriately does not identify an ingredient.
The task is understandable independently; its diagnosis-to-test association and noncompetitive alternatives are easier than the requested resident decision.
suggestions: Supply the observed onset/course without inventing a diagnostic cutoff.
Compare credible investigations for the actual candidate exposures and clinical mechanisms at the same stage; replace prospective tryptase testing as a disposable foil.

title: Closure materials after relevant patch testing
clarityIssues: 'Prior adhesive ingredient' and 'alternative adhesive' are generic labels. A resident cannot assess ingredient relationships beyond the author-supplied tested/untested categories.

cues.phrase: the dermatologist judged clinically relevant
cues.why: Together with the explicitly ingredient-containing original dressing, this supplies the interpretation and the exclusion rule.

cues.phrase: The proposed nylon suture material tested negative.
cues.why: The only explicitly negative closure material paired with the explicitly ingredient-free dressing yields the key by a nonmedical safe/unsafe matrix.

cues.phrase: it was not included in the test session
cues.why: The untested alternative is an overtly marked uncertainty beside the uniquely fully evaluated plan.

fairness: Nylon with gauze is the best supported offered plan; avoiding the known relevant allergen is appropriate. A negative test should not be taught as a universal guarantee of tolerability.

The four combinations balance component frequency and avoid convergence, but both component choices are directly stated. The first node already teaches that specialist testing must establish relevance.
The later task is coherent and understandable from its own update/exhibit; the limitation is depth rather than sequence continuity.
suggestions: Use concrete supported product/ingredient information and a real residual interpretation problem rather than tested-negative versus explicitly unknown.
If retained as simple allergen-avoidance practice, seek explicit basic-purpose acceptance rather than labeling two matching exclusions as two-step reasoning.

title: Perioperative reaction with population-normal acute tryptase
clarityIssues: A baseline sample is said to be available but neither paired values nor collection chronology is provided. The instruction to interpret the 'actual paired record' cannot be followed from the displayed data.
The task asks for an interpretation, but the key is a workup action and the other options are causal classifications.

cues.phrase: Retain a perioperative hypersensitivity workup
cues.why: The key is the only cautious action beside two definitive diagnoses.

cues.phrase: proven drug-specific IgE allergy
cues.why: 'Proven' is an unsupported certainty cue when no drug-specific testing has been shown.

fairness: The clinical syndrome warrants evaluation despite a population-normal acute tryptase. The intended key is defensible; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The available-but-hidden baseline is decorative unless the question actually requires paired interpretation. Missing data must not be used to simulate difficulty.
This first node stands alone; its feedback should not be expanded to teach the exact exposure-scope answer of the next node.
suggestions: Compare three interpretations or three specific workup plans at the same level of certainty.
Either remove the unused baseline claim or provide a supported paired record and ask a consequence that genuinely depends on interpreting it; do not invent a threshold.
Keep the reusable point that a reference-range result does not rule out the clinical event.

title: Scope of perioperative hypersensitivity assessment
clarityIssues: 'Drug, preparation and coated-device testing' can imply validated testing of every item or the device itself. The more qualified explanation describes specialist assessment of plausible culprits and variable test validity.

cues.phrase: the skin-preparation and device pages were not attached
cues.why: A named omission tells the learner exactly which components to add.

cues.phrase: Drug, preparation and coated-device testing
cues.why: The key is a strict superset of the other scopes and uniquely repeats all exhibit categories. A nonmedical reader can select the most comprehensive list.

fairness: Including plausible nonintravenous exposures is appropriate. The exact testing method and validity must remain specialist decisions rather than an instruction to test every listed object indiscriminately.
The first node already lists antibiotic, neuromuscular blocker, anesthetic drugs and preparation products. The second node's omission-repair question adds little independent inference.
The later task is coherent with the case, but if selected independently it should retain a concise description of the immediate systemic event rather than rely only on a generic 'post-event' label.
suggestions: Compare equally complete, credible assessment strategies whose selection depends on actual chronology or exposure evidence, rather than nested lists.
Use accurate language for specialist evaluation of candidate agents and relevant device ingredients, preserving uncertainty about available tests.

title: Perioperative product avoidance and the iodine label

cues.phrase: Avoid chlorhexidine exposure
cues.why: The exhibit explicitly instructs the learner to remove the ingredient that labels three of the four option combinations through the preparation or coating.

cues.phrase: An uncoated catheter with appropriate procedural specifications is listed.
cues.why: This announces that the desired replacement is suitable, leaving no residual device-selection decision.

cues.phrase: Chlorhexidine preparation and the coated catheter
cues.why: This option violates the explicitly supplied avoidance instruction twice and is not a credible near-miss.

fairness: The intended povidone-iodine/uncoated-device combination is defensible: shrimp allergy does not establish iodine or povidone-iodine allergy, and the confirmed chlorhexidine allergy applies to coated devices too.

The balanced matrix prevents frequency convergence, but a nonmedical avoidance rule can solve it without resolving the shrimp misconception. The preceding node already highlights preparation and coated-device exposures.
The node supplies the diagnosis and product map needed to stand alone. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
suggestions: Make the seafood-label interpretation consequential by providing credible choices that do not all but one violate an explicit ingredient prohibition.

Keep the established allergy as legitimate management context, but remove the repeated pre-answer instruction and availability reassurance; compare equally allergen-aware plans where the remaining difference matters.

title: Investigation of persistent glove-associated eczema

cues.phrase: the product rubber chemicals were not tested
cues.why: This names the missing test target and uniquely matches the rubber-chemical key.

cues.phrase: Repeat serum latex-protein specific-IgE testing
cues.why: The displayed negative assay and unchanged delayed symptoms give no reason to repeat it; together with the other immediate-latex option, the key is the only different mechanism category.

fairness: Exposure-directed patch testing is reasonable for persistent eczematous symptoms across natural rubber and nitrile. The findings support investigation, not a proven allergic rather than irritant diagnosis.
Recognizing delayed eczema and matching patch testing is a single familiar mechanism-to-test chain. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified in this node.
The negative latex-protein IgE result must be preserved accurately in the subsequent case history.
suggestions: Remove the named-omission sentence and compare credible next assessments for unresolved glove dermatitis.
Use the prior negative assay as evidence with limits rather than as a reason to make both distractors immediate-latex tests.

title: A new immediate event after prior glove dermatitis
clarityIssues: The earlier node explicitly reports negative serum latex-protein specific IgE, but this node says the available prior report 'contains no immediate protein-sensitization results'. If these are different documents, that distinction is unstated; the sequence otherwise appears contradictory.

cues.phrase: appeared rapidly
cues.why: The sole 'Immediate-allergy assessment' option directly matches the new timing; both alternatives repeat delayed patch testing.

cues.phrase: Earlier symptoms were persistent scaly plaques.
cues.why: Together with the explicitly 'delayed allergy' label, the exhibit preclassifies the old mechanism and makes the old-versus-new timing contrast elementary.

fairness: A newly documented rapid multisystem reaction warrants immediate-hypersensitivity evaluation even after a prior delayed contact allergy. The intended action is sound; the explanation appropriately avoids proving a specific IgE culprit from the event alone.
The new-event exhibit is self-contained, but the contradiction about earlier testing damages full-case coherence. Do not silently erase the earlier negative result to make the new decision easier.
The preceding explanation already teaches the distinction between latex-protein assays and delayed rubber-chemical reactions, further reducing this node's independent difficulty.
suggestions: Reconcile the record explicitly: retain the prior negative assay and its chronology, or identify which report lacked that result. Do not imply an old negative excludes a later event.
Compare credible assessment plans for the new immediate event rather than one immediate workup against two repeated delayed tests.

title: Persistent elbow restriction after scar therapy
fairness: The changing skin-band tension at the shared passive/active endpoint, persistent restriction despite therapy and absence of an osseous block support addressing the scar. Capsular and tendon procedures target plausible alternative restraints but lack equivalent positive evidence here.

Normal alignment alone does not exclude capsular contracture; the positive skin findings, not the radiograph alone, support the intended target. The task's 'should be considered' and the explanation's specialist-design limitation appropriately avoid guaranteeing a specific rearrangement.
Localization followed by selection of a reconstructive target constitutes two consequential steps. The standalone story is coherent; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

title: Sampling an enlarging lesion beside a scar

cues.phrase: new growing scar-end lesion
cues.why: This uniquely repeats the task's 'enlarging nodule'; the other choices explicitly examine a different, flat site.

cues.phrase: opposite end of the old linear scar
cues.why: This makes the sampling mismatch unmistakable. Both distractors repeat work on that same wrong site, so even a nonmedical reader can choose the new target.

fairness: Representative biopsy of the enlarging eroded lesion is appropriate. Benign tissue from another site does not establish its identity; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The current option set is a location-matching exercise, not a difficult evidence-adequacy decision. The task is otherwise complete and standalone.
suggestions: Retain the important principle of representative sampling, but compare plausible ways to investigate the actual lesion rather than repeat an explicitly wrong site.
If using a specimen map, make the distinction between sampled and unsampled components consequential without hiding the acquisition information needed for one best answer.

title: Persistent symptomatic scar bulk after topical care
clarityIssues: 'Through a documented course' does not establish adequate duration or response trajectory. Without that information, continuing silicone is not fully ranked against escalation. No arbitrary duration should be invented.

cues.phrase: Silicone gel was used as directed
cues.why: The next-treatment question pits the new intervention against repetition of the already described inadequate treatment.

cues.phrase: Shoulder and elbow motion are full; the skin moves freely
cues.why: This explicitly removes the reason for the only operative competitor, leaving injection as the sole unexcluded option.

fairness: Intralesional triamcinolone is a reasonable treatment for persistent symptomatic keloidal scar bulk. The explanation appropriately avoids claiming universal superiority over all scar therapies.
The intended ranking is plausible, but adequacy of conservative treatment should be established if failure of that treatment is the deciding feature. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The standalone sequence is clear; it currently uses treatment-failed/function-normal exclusions rather than a close therapeutic choice.
suggestions: Provide a source-supported description establishing the completed conservative trial, without adding an invented cutoff.
Replace the contracture procedure with a clinically credible scar-bulk treatment and supply supported patient-specific information that makes one best.

title: Planning another excision for recurrent earlobe keloid
clarityIssues: The task asks what should be discussed, while the explanation reserves radiotherapy suitability and alternatives for later review. Clarify whether the objective is the need for an adjunct or selection of this particular adjunct.

cues.phrase: Excision with planned adjuvant radiotherapy
cues.why: This is the only option adding recurrence-directed adjunctive therapy; the others change margin or coverage after repeated surgery-only recurrence.

fairness: Discussing excision with adjuvant radiotherapy is defensible in this recurrent adult earlobe case. I do not identify it as a confident clinical error.

The choices do not establish that radiotherapy outranks other credible adjunctive specialist regimens, and the explanation itself limits that claim. The no-adjunct foils chiefly test the familiar rule that excision alone recurs.
Standalone chronology is coherent. Do not turn the discussion answer into a universal requirement for radiotherapy.
suggestions: Either ask the narrower adjunct-planning principle as an explicitly accepted basic item, or compare credible combined regimens with clinician-supported selection factors.
Align the option and explanation on what is actually being endorsed; retain uncertainty about individual radiotherapy suitability.

title: Operative assessment of acute flap deterioration
clarityIssues: The opposite limb remaining warm is not strong evidence about arterial supply of the affected limb. It adds distracting reassurance rather than resolving the proximal-supply competitor.

cues.phrase: The arterial signal persisted; the venous signal changed.
cues.why: The abnormality's vascular label directly matches the venous option; the raw color/refill/bleeding observations are no longer needed to localize the problem.

cues.phrase: Which operative assessment
cues.why: The task supplies the exploration decision, leaving only a vessel-label classification rather than recognition followed by an urgent management choice.

fairness: The congested flap warrants urgent microsurgical assessment/exploration; venous outflow is the best initial target. The explanation correctly avoids claiming that the exact lesion is identified.
A preserved arterial signal does not guarantee adequate tissue perfusion, but the combined findings support the intended answer. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
This first node is coherent as retrospective review. Its explanation introduces the phase distinction used later without naming leech treatment.
suggestions: Test a real urgent management decision using the raw flap findings, or seek explicit acceptance as basic vascular-pattern recognition.
Use relevant ipsilateral findings if limb-level supply is a serious competitor; remove the opposite-limb reassurance.
Do not hide necessary monitoring findings merely to manufacture difficulty; change the decision structure instead.

title: Residual distal congestion after flap exploration
clarityIssues: The task requests an 'adjunct', but repeating operative anastomotic revision is a different decision category.

cues.phrase: becomes softer when congested blood is released at the surface
cues.why: This pre-demonstrates the surface-offloading mechanism of the leech option.

cues.phrase: Repeat revision of the patent drainage anastomosis
cues.why: The option embeds the reason it is wrong in 'patent'; the exhibit also explicitly removes a kink, compressive collection and further drainage target.

cues.phrase: Monitored medicinal-leech venous offloading
cues.why: This is uniquely qualified as monitored and uniquely repeats the venous mechanism; the competing surgical option is additionally prefiltered by 'adjunct'.

fairness: Selected medicinal-leech therapy after correction or exclusion of surgically remediable outflow problems is plausible. Offline review cannot establish that the exact distal free-flap anatomy makes it superior to every specialist alternative; this is a clinician-review uncertainty, not a confident error.

The new exploration results materially distinguish this stage from initial urgent exploration and make the node understandable independently. However, the mechanism is demonstrated and the nearest operative competitor is explicitly invalidated, so the question stops short of two consequential steps.
General flap-congestion recognition is high yield; this precise post-revision small-paddle adjunct selection is more specialist than a core commonly tested resident concept.
suggestions: Use a neutral next-management task and remove explanatory qualifiers from the options.

Have the clinician establish the actual supported boundary between further surgery and temporary offloading; compare credible choices at that boundary without removing safety-critical exploration findings.
If retained, ensure post-answer teaching addresses the need for specialist infection-prevention and blood-loss monitoring protocols without inventing drugs, doses or intervals.

title: Systemic symptoms during medicinal-leech treatment

cues.phrase: ongoing bleeding at the treated sites
cues.why: Together with orthostatic symptoms and tachycardia, this names the problem for which the only blood-count option is an obvious match.

cues.phrase: No systemic anticoagulant was started
cues.why: This appears designed to delete the INR distractor, although anticoagulant exposure is not the only reason coagulation testing might be relevant.

cues.phrase: The paddle is less swollen, with improved surface color.
cues.why: This directly weakens the only local-flap investigation, leaving a straightforward systemic blood-loss test.

fairness: A CBC/hemoglobin trend is appropriate to assess ongoing blood loss, and the question asks an investigation rather than implying that laboratory testing replaces immediate clinical assessment.
No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Lack of systemic anticoagulant use does not establish normal coagulation, and the explanation should not teach that implication.

The later stage is coherent and supplies enough context independently. Improved local viability versus new systemic symptoms is useful, but the alternatives are too weak to create two consequential steps.
suggestions: Remove the unsupported anticoagulant-to-INR elimination scaffold and compare plausible assessments for a genuinely unresolved systemic complication.
If preserved as blood-loss safety recognition, label and obtain acceptance for that intentionally easy role.

title: Initial closure strategy for a contaminated wound

cues.phrase: Visible grit remained
cues.why: Both distractors propose immediate closure after exactly this inadequate cleansing; the key is the only option that addresses the conspicuously unresolved problem.

cues.phrase: Open wound care with debridement and reassessment
cues.why: This is the uniquely comprehensive plan against two near-duplicate immediate-approximation techniques.

fairness: Further debridement/open management and reassessment are appropriate for retained material and a dusky nonbleeding edge. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The findings are important and should not be deleted to make immediate closure seem reasonable. The problem is the absence of a credible competing strategy.
The first retrospective stage stands alone. Its explanation sets up reassessment but does not itself dictate whether the later wound will be ready to close.
suggestions: Replace one closure-material duplicate with a credible wound-management strategy and make the actual remaining contamination/viability assessment drive the distinction.
Alternatively seek explicit basic/safety acceptance; do not call 'dirty wound, leave open' a hard two-step decision.

title: Closure after serial wound preparation

cues.phrase: Both edges bleed and approximate freely without blanching or excessive tension.
cues.why: The exhibit essentially demonstrates direct closure readiness rather than leaving an unresolved plan to compare.

cues.phrase: No tissue gap or exposed deep structure remains
cues.why: This explicitly removes the skin-graft competitor while the uniformly viable bed removes further excisional debridement.

fairness: Delayed primary closure is a reasonable best answer on these observations. No exact day is needed merely to apply the observed readiness criteria, and no arbitrary timing cutoff should be added.

The later findings genuinely differ from the initial contaminated assessment, and the update supplies prior open care/debridement so the node stands alone. However, every offered competitor is explicitly negated.
The prior explanation already promises debridement and reassessment. The follow-up is coherent but functions as confirmation of that plan rather than a difficult new decision.
suggestions: Retain the decision-critical viability, infection and edge information, but compare realistic competing closure/healing plans whose ranking requires interpretation of current geometry and course.
If the intended purpose is simple recognition of delayed primary closure, obtain explicit basic-purpose acceptance rather than claiming two consequential steps.
